kind: Owned synthetic operational handbook, not real user documents; frozen query labels, not a general retrieval benchmark

documents.text: A read timeout means the client stopped waiting for socket data. It does not prove the remote server did not execute the request.
Commit a complete user assistant pair only after validation. Candidate history is private until the version check succeeds.
Read only tools use a fixed allowlist and a bounded call budget. Unknown tools and invalid arguments are rejected before execution.
Cancellation requests interruption. A worker that ignores interruption can finish later. A timeout is not forced termination.
Structured output must pass syntax and field validation. Parse success alone cannot establish semantic correctness.
KV cache stores projected keys and values for attention. Cached positions continue increasing after eviction.
Retrieval returns ranked evidence chunks. A source identifier and exact quote make the selected evidence traceable.
A gripper release command does not prove object placement. Check contact separation, tray support, location and speed.
A retry can repeat an operation already executed remotely. Read only lookup is easier to retry than a payment.
Keep API keys in server environment variables. Never embed credentials in browser code or evidence logs.
